threads.title: Your total loss settlement, claim LR-26-118204

exchanges.author: worker
exchanges.subject: Your total loss settlement, claim LR-26-118204
exchanges.body: Dear Ms. Nunez, as discussed, your 2014 Toyota Corolla LE is a total loss (repair estimate $9,140 exceeds its value). Actual cash value $8,260 (CCC valuation attached: base $8,420, condition +$150, mileage -$310), less your $1,000 deductible: $7,260. Texas Dow Employees Credit Union's payoff of $5,140 is paid to them; $2,120 to you. To accept, sign the attached title and power of attorney forms; we pay within 5 business days of acceptance. If you disagree, send comparable listings and I'll review them, or either of us may request appraisal under your policy. Your rental is covered up to $30 a day (maximum $900). Maribel Ochoa

threads.title: Your claim LR-26-117730: settlement demand above your policy limit

exchanges.author: worker
exchanges.subject: Your claim LR-26-117730: settlement demand above your policy limit
exchanges.body: Dear Mr. Prewitt, we've received a demand from the attorney for Kayla Simmons offering to settle her injury claim against you for your $30,000 bodily injury limit, with a full release of you, if accepted by Friday, November 6 at 5:00 p.m. Her claimed damages exceed your limit, so you could be personally responsible for any amount above it if the claim isn't settled. We are reviewing the demand promptly and will let you know our decision before the deadline. You may consult a personal attorney at your own expense. Please call me with any questions. Maribel Ochoa, Leon River Mutual, 254-555-0180

threads.title: Policy-limits demand, time-limited to Fri 11/6 5 p.m.: LR-26-117730 (Simmons v. Prewitt)

exchanges.author: worker
exchanges.subject: Policy-limits demand, time-limited to Fri 11/6 5 p.m.: LR-26-117730 (Simmons v. Prewitt)
exchanges.body: Wade, Rena: Keel Injury Law demands the $30,000 BI limit for Kayla Simmons in exchange for a full release of our insured, Dale Prewitt; the offer expires Friday 11/6 at 5:00 p.m. CT. Liability is clear (insured rear-ended her, cited). Billed and estimated specials $41,850 (incl. $20,000 estimated injections) plus $4,600 lost wages: well above the limit. This looks like a demand an ordinarily prudent insurer would accept (Stowers). I recommend tendering limits. Reserve is $12,000; I'm requesting an increase to $30,000 (above my authority). Can we take it to Wednesday's large loss committee? Copies of the demand and records are in the file.

exchanges.author: worker
exchanges.subject: SIU referral: LR-26-118281 (Ostrowski), hail 10/29
exchanges.body: Referral: LR-26-118281, Glen Ostrowski, 2016 Nissan Altima, hail claimed for 10/29. Indicators: all six photos he submitted have EXIF capture dates of 5/19/2026; ISO ClaimSearch shows a 2025-04-02 hail claim on the same VIN paid by Brazos Valley ($3,870) with no repair record. I haven't raised either with the insured. I'll keep handling (acknowledgment and an in-person inspection request) unless you advise otherwise. Maribel

threads.title: Inbound call, Carla Nunez (hail total loss)

exchanges.author: c_insured2
exchanges.body: Hi, this is Carla Nunez. The appraiser said my Corolla is totaled from the hail. What happens now and how much will I get? I still owe on it.

exchanges.author: worker
exchanges.body: I'm sorry about your car, Ms. Nunez. The valuation puts its actual cash value at eight thousand two hundred sixty dollars. After your one-thousand-dollar deductible, the settlement is seven thousand two hundred sixty. Your credit union's payoff is five thousand one hundred forty, so that goes to them first and the remaining two thousand one hundred twenty comes to you.

exchanges.author: c_insured2
exchanges.body: That seems low. Can I see how you got that?

exchanges.author: worker
exchanges.body: Absolutely. I'm emailing you the full valuation report today. If you find comparable cars for sale that you think we missed, send them to me and I'll review them. You also have the right to an appraisal under your policy if we can't agree.
